title_vi: Redis lưu dữ liệu xuống đĩa thế nào?

related.reason_vi: Lưu xuống đĩa là bước đầu trong quá trình phát triển kiến trúc Redis.
Redis nhanh vì giữ dữ liệu trong bộ nhớ; bài này nói cái giá phải trả để dữ liệu đó không mất.

claims.evidence: Every statement was checked against the Redis persistence page of redis/docs at commit 3b030c7ef066c0bb7f88ddec02c784e49783b0f8, the Redis 7.0.15 source (aof.c, server.c, redis.conf at f35f36a265403c07b119830aa4bb3b7d71653ec9), all read from partial clones, and against an experiment run on 2026-10-18 with the Ubuntu redis-server 7.0.15 package (scratch script: no persistence, RDB after BGSAVE, AOF everysec; 1500 keys; kill -9; restart; DBSIZE).

claims.claim_vi: RDB takes point-in-time snapshots; AOF logs every write operation and replays it at startup; persistence can be disabled or both combined.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of redis/docs at that commit.

claims.claim_vi: Normally the AOF buffer is written to the file in beforeSleep before replies are sent (flushAppendOnlyFile runs before handleClientsWithPendingWritesUsingThreads); with appendfsync everysec and a background fsync still running, the write may be postponed for up to about two seconds while replies still go out; only appendfsync always guarantees write and fsync before the reply.
claims.verified_by: Read the 7.0.15 source: when postponed, flushAppendOnlyFile returns early and beforeSleep goes on to handleClientsWithPendingWritesUsingThreads; the latency page describes the delayed write(2).

claims.claim_vi: appendfsync always fsyncs before sending replies (one write and one fsync per batch); everysec fsyncs every second in a background thread and may lose about one second of writes in a disaster; no leaves flushing to the operating system.
claims.section: How durable is the append only file?
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of redis/docs at that commit.

claims.claim_vi: RDB snapshotting forks a child that writes a temporary file and replaces the old one, relying on copy-on-write; fork can stop Redis serving clients for milliseconds up to a second on big datasets.
claims.verified_by: Read; the experiment's log showed 'Background saving started by pid', 'DB saved on disk' and 'Fork CoW for RDB: current 0 MB'.

claims.claim_vi: Experiment, Redis 7.0.15, 1500 keys then kill -9: no persistence kept 0 keys; RDB saved at 1000 keys kept 1000; AOF everysec kept 1500.
claims.verified_by: Own experiment with the Ubuntu redis-server 7.0.15 package; the URL is the configuration file of that version whose settings were varied.

claims.claim_vi: Since 7.0 the AOF is a base file plus incremental files tracked by a manifest; with aof-use-rdb-preamble yes the rewritten base is in RDB format; when both exist, Redis loads the AOF at startup; a truncated last command is discarded when aof-load-truncated is yes.
claims.section: Append-only file; Interactions between AOF and RDB persistence; redis.conf APPEND ONLY MODE
claims.verified_by: Read; the experiment listed appendonly.aof.1.base.rdb, appendonly.aof.1.incr.aof and the manifest, and after BGREWRITEAOF appendonly.aof.2.base.rdb starting with the bytes REDIS.

claims.claim_vi: Default RDB save points in 7.0 are 3600 s/1 change, 300 s/100 changes, 60 s/10000 changes; appendonly defaults to no; appendfsync defaults to everysec.
Redis docs recommend both methods for strong data safety, RDB alone when a few minutes of loss is acceptable, and discourage AOF alone; RDB restarts faster than AOF with big datasets.

design_notes_vi: Ba phần: bốn bước của một lệnh ghi khi bật AOF, ba kết quả thử nghiệm sau kill -9, bốn điều cần nhớ. Vẽ bằng scripts/figures, không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: Source says persistence is not on the critical path and does not block writes; the lesson notes that fork() can pause Redis and that appendfsync always makes replies wait for fsync.

Source presents AOF write-after logging without saying when the file is written; the lesson adds, from the Redis source, that the buffer is normally written before replies are sent, that everysec may postpone that write while replies go out, and separates write() from fsync.
Lesson adds an experiment (kill -9 under three settings) and the multi-part AOF of Redis 7.0, which the source does not cover; it states that killing the process is not a power failure.
